headline_marked: [[Mirpur health center]] razed, looted by 200 attackers; vaccines destroyed
headline: Mirpur health center razed, looted by 200 attackers; vaccines destroyed
summary: A private healthcare center in Mirpur was vandalized and looted by over 200 masked individuals. The attack destroyed essential medical equipment, vaccines, and medicines, raising concerns amid rising measles and dengue outbreaks.
details: Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked the Radda MCH-FP Center in Mirpur late Thursday night. The attackers reportedly held security guards hostage, looted valuable medical equipment, medicines, and vaccines, and then demolished the facility, including a concrete and three semi-concrete buildings, using heavy machinery.

The Democratic Rights Committee condemned the brutal incident, stating it was a terrorist attack not just on a building but on public health and the right to life. They highlighted the timing, with the country already grappling with measles outbreaks and a severe dengue epidemic, making the destruction of a vital Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) center particularly alarming.

The clinic's executive director, Nasrin Akhtar, reported damages exceeding 10 million Bangladeshi Taka. A case was filed with the Shah Ali Police Station, leading to the arrest of four individuals who have since been sent to jail. The attack was allegedly carried out under the banner of an organization called 'Shomomona Dokandar Somobay Somity Limited' ( সমমনা দোকানদার সমবায় সমিতি লিমিটেড).

The Democratic Rights Committee's statement pointed to the involvement of local BNP leader Hanif Miah and the 'Shomomona Dokandar Somobay Somity Limited' signboard as evidence of a well-planned land-grabbing operation under political patronage. They expressed grave concern that the incident occurred despite the presence of law enforcement, calling it a dangerous precedent for state security and impunity.

The committee demanded the immediate arrest and swift trial of all perpetrators, including Hanif Miah, and called for departmental and legal action against the Shah Ali Police Station OC and other police personnel present during the attack for their alleged inaction. They also called for the recovery of the encroached land and the prompt reconstruction of the clinic to resume services for vulnerable mothers and children.

The organization urged all conscientious citizens to build a strong movement against such attacks on healthcare services, emphasizing that the destruction of health centers for the benefit of mafias, land grabbers, and political beneficiaries is unacceptable in a civilized society or democratic state. They vowed to resist any attack on the people's right to health and treatment.

headline_marked: 5 madrasa students [[burnt by 33,000-volt power line]] in Fatullah
headline: 5 madrasa students burnt by 33,000-volt power line in Fatullah
summary: Five girls aged 11-14 were electrocuted while playing on the roof of Mahela Khatun Women’s Madrasa after sugarcane touched a high-voltage line.
details: Five students of Mahela Khatun Women’s Madrasa in Narayanganj's Fatullah were severely burnt on Saturday evening after an electrical accident on the rooftop.
The victims, aged between 11 and 14, are identified as Zidni (14), Lamia (13), Sumaiya (13), Achhia (12), and Atia (11).
Officials say the students were playing on the roof of the four-storey building with sugarcane, which accidentally touched a 33,000-volt power line running over the roof, triggering a flash and fire.
Zidni suffered burns to 82 percent of her body, while Lamia, Atia, and Sumaiya were burnt over 55, 45, and 13 percent of their bodies respectively.
The injured were first taken to Narayanganj General Hospital for emergency care before being transferred to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka.
Fire Service and Civil Defence officials noted that a gas riser on the building's ground floor also exploded during the incident, though no major damage was reported on the ground floor.
caption:
A piece of sugarcane touched a 33,000-volt power line, leaving five young madrasa students severely burnt.

The injured were first taken to Narayanganj General Hospital for emergency care before being transferred to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka.
